desc:
A social network has n users numbered 0 to n - 1, with no friendships at the start. A pair [x, y] in restrictions means that x and y must never be connected, neither directly nor through a chain of friends.

The friend requests requests[k] = [u, v] are handled one by one in order. A request is approved if, after making u and v friends, no restricted pair would be connected; otherwise it is rejected and nothing changes. An approved request makes the friendship permanent. A request between users who are already connected (directly or indirectly) is always approved.

Return an array with 1 for each approved request and 0 for each rejected one.

n = 4
restrictions = [[0,3]]
requests = [[0,1],[1,2],[2,3],[3,1]]

result = [1,1,0,0]

After the first two requests {0,1,2} are connected. Linking 2 and 3 would connect 0 with 3, so it is rejected, and so is 3-1 for the same reason.
constraints: All pairs have two different users in the range [0, n - 1]
hints: After a request you may need to know whether any restricted pair has become connected. Checking the whole graph with a BFS each time is wasteful.
Only the merge of the two components of u and v can create a violation. You can test the hypothetical merge without performing it.

Keep a union-find. For a request with different roots ru, rv, look at every restriction (x, y): if {find(x), find(y)} == {ru, rv} the merge would connect a forbidden pair, so reject. Otherwise union and approve.
editorial: A restriction can only be violated at the moment two components are merged, and the only way to violate (x, y) by merging components A and B is that x is in one of them and y in the other. So for a request with ru = find(u) != rv = find(v) we scan the restrictions and reject if some pair has its two roots equal to {ru, rv} (in either order). If no restriction blocks it, we union the sets and answer 1.

If the roots are already equal the request changes nothing and is approved. The scan costs O(R) per request, so the total is O(Q · R · α(n)), about 160,000 find operations at the stated limits. For much larger inputs you could store, per component, the set of components it is forbidden from joining and merge these sets small-to-large; the plain scan is the standard solution at these sizes.
